input.strategy_title: Bring-your-own vector database for RAG workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RAG applications built on Llama Stack need a vector store, and today the
platform neither ships one nor documents how to attach an external one.
Customers are split into two camps with incompatible expectations: regulated
customers want a platform-managed vector database with supported images and
lifecycle, while cloud-native customers already run managed services (e.g.
a cloud vector DB) and only want a sanctioned way to connect them. We have not
decided which posture to productize first, and the answer changes most of the
downstream work.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the first supported vector store posture: platform-managed (operator-deployed Milvus) versus external-connection-only. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Depending on that decision: either administrators can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images, or data scientists can register an external vector store connection per project with validated connectivity. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | The Dashboard exposes the chosen integration (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path, or connection management UI for the external path). |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation covers setup and limits for whichever posture ships. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- Shipping both postures in the same release
- Embedding model selection and lifecycle (separate strategy)

## Open Questions

1. Managed Milvus versus external-connection-only is genuinely undecided — the
   evaluation in HLR-1 must weigh supportability cost, disconnected-environment
   viability, and time-to-market, and the outcome forks the implementation
   structure for HLR-2 through HLR-5.

# Midstream onboarding of the Milvus repository

## Description

Creates the midstream home for the Milvus vector database source under
opendatahub-io so the platform can build productized Milvus container images.
This is the repository onboarding step of bringing a new upstream component
into the platform for the managed vector store posture; the build pipeline and
operator deployment capabilities build on it. Applies only if the
platform-managed posture is selected.

## Scope

- Fork or import the identified upstream Milvus release into a midstream
  repository under the opendatahub-io organization.
- Establish the branching and rebasing workflow used by other midstream
  repositories, including documenting how upstream releases are tracked.
- Verify the source builds from a clean checkout at the pinned upstream
  version, and record build instructions.
- Register the repository with the platform's midstream conventions (owners,
  branch protection, CI triggers where applicable).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A midstream Milvus repository exists under opendatahub-io, seeded from a
  pinned upstream release that is recorded in the repository.
- The documented branching/rebasing workflow is written down and a first rebase
  or sync from upstream has been exercised successfully.
- The repository builds from a clean checkout following only its documented
  instructions.
- Repository conventions (ownership, branch protection) are configured.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, managed path): enables "productized images" for the
  operator-deployed managed vector store.

## Notes

- Milvus is a new component for the platform — it has no architecture-context
  file and is not a canonical RHAI Jira component; this work is filed under the
  Platform Operator component as the deploying and lifecycle-owning surface.
- This epic runs in parallel with license validation of Milvus and its
  transitive dependencies; neither blocks the other.

# License validation for Milvus and transitive dependencies

## Description

Runs license scanning and clearance for Milvus and its transitive dependencies
so the platform can ship productized Milvus images in the managed vector store
posture. The scan determines whether the dependency set is license-compatible
with platform productization; a failure here changes the approach or the
dependency set before operator deployment work proceeds. Applies only if the
platform-managed posture is selected.

## Scope

- Run the platform's license scanning process over the pinned upstream Milvus
  release and its full transitive dependency tree.
- Check every detected license against the platform's allowed-license policy.
- Produce a license scan report with a clear pass/fail summary and, for any
  flagged license, the remediation options (alternative dependency, upstream
  change, exclusion).
- Record the clearance decision for the scanned version so image
  productization can proceed on a known-good basis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A complete license scan report exists for the pinned Milvus release and its
  transitive dependencies.
- Every license found is classified against the platform's allowed-license
  policy, with the classification traceable in the report.
- All flagged licenses have documented remediation options, and the overall
  result is a recorded go/no-go for productizing the scanned version.
- The scan is reproducible from the recorded inputs (version pin, scanner
  configuration).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, managed path): productized images for the managed vector store
  require a license-cleared dependency set.

## Notes

- This epic runs in parallel with the midstream repository onboarding; it does
  not wait for the repository to exist (it scans the pinned upstream release).
- Operator deployment of the managed vector store must not start until this
  clearance completes, because a license failure changes the dependency set and
  the approach.

## Description

Onboards the midstream Milvus repository to Konflux so the platform produces
buildable, released container images for the managed vector store. This
delivers the build pipeline for productized Milvus images; it does not block
the operator deployment work, which proceeds in parallel and is gated instead
by acceptance criteria on image availability. Applies only if the
platform-managed posture is selected.

## Scope

- Create the Konflux onboarding configuration for the midstream Milvus
  repository, following the standard known-recipe used for other platform
  components.
- Wire image builds for the pinned Milvus version into the pipeline, including
  the image build and push configuration used for platform releases.
- Verify the pipeline runs end to end on the repository's default branch and
  produces publishable image artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Konflux onboarding configuration for the midstream Milvus repository is
  merged and active.
- The build pipeline produces Milvus container images from the midstream
  repository without manual intervention beyond the documented triggers.
- A full pipeline run on the default branch completes green, and the resulting
  images are pushed to the registry the platform uses for released images.

  managed vector store.

  needs a repository to build from).
- The operator deployment work runs in parallel with this epic; its
  first-execution gate is the availability of a green build pipeline and pinned
  image digests, captured as acceptance criteria there rather than as a
  scheduling dependency.

# Managed vector store deployment via the Platform Operator

## Description

Extends the Platform Operator so administrators can deploy and lifecycle the
platform-managed Milvus vector store with productized images, delivering the
managed half of HLR-2: regulated customers get a platform-managed vector
database with supported images and lifecycle. Applies only if the
platform-managed posture is selected.

## Scope

- Add the managed vector store as a deployable, lifecycle-managed operand of
  the Platform Operator: deployment, readiness, and reconciliation to desired
  state.
- Reference the productized Milvus images by pinned digest from the platform's
  released-image registry.
- Provide the administrator-facing deployment controls at the functional level
  the strategy states: an administrator can deploy the managed vector store
  through the Platform Operator.
- Ensure deletion and re-creation of the managed vector store works cleanly
  (lifecycle coverage per the strategy's "supported images and lifecycle"
  language).

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform
  Operator, and the store reaches a ready/usable state without manual pod
  surgery.
- The deployment uses the productized Milvus images by pinned digest from the
  platform image registry, and the digest is available at deployment time (the
  build pipeline for the productized images is green on the midstream
  repository).
- The operator reconciles the managed vector store to desired state: deleting
  and re-creating the store, and recovering from induced failure of its
  components, converges back to ready.
- The deployment works with the platform's standard configuration surfaces (no
  hand-edited manifests required beyond documented administrator input).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, managed path): "administrators can deploy the managed vector
  store through the Platform Operator with productized images."

## Notes

- This epic must not start before Milvus license validation completes: a
  license failure changes the dependency set and the approach.
- This epic runs in parallel with the Konflux onboarding of the Milvus build
  pipeline; the coupling is enforced by the pinned-digest and green-pipeline
  acceptance criteria above, not by a scheduling dependency.
- The Platform Operator has no architecture-context file; the implementing team
  should confirm existing operand-deployment patterns before designing the
  integration.
- The Llama Stack provider wiring and the Dashboard deploy-and-manage UI build
  on the operand/connection surface this epic defines.

# Llama Stack consumption of the managed vector store as RAG provider

## Description

Wires Llama Stack distributions to consume the platform-managed Milvus vector
store as their RAG vector provider without hand-editing distribution configs,
delivering HLR-3 on the managed path. Data scientists building RAG applications
on Llama Stack get a working vector provider backed by the platform-managed
store. Applies only if the platform-managed posture is selected.

## Scope

- Configure Llama Stack distributions to use the platform-managed vector store
  as the vector/RAG provider through the distribution's provider-plugin model
  (per the Llama Stack architecture: provider plugins configured per
  distribution), without hand-editing distribution config files.
- Expose the managed store's connection details to distributions through the
  platform's standard configuration surfaces rather than manual edits.
- Verify end-to-end RAG behavior through the distribution: document
  ingestion and retrieval against the managed store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution can be brought up using the platform-managed
  vector store as its RAG vector provider with no hand-edited distribution
  config files — configuration flows through the platform's standard surfaces.
- A documented RAG round trip works end to end: documents ingested through the
  distribution's RAG API are retrievable in queries, backed by the managed
  store.
- The provider wiring works against a store deployed through the Platform
  Operator's managed deployment capability (the operand/connection surface the
  operator defines).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): "Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store
  as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs" — managed-path
  coverage.

## Notes

- Builds on the operand/connection surface defined by the Platform Operator's
  managed vector store deployment; that surface must exist before this wiring
  can be built and verified against it.
- The Llama Stack architecture lists "Milvus/vector providers for RAG
  workflows (optional)" as a dependency — the provider-plugin model exists
  upstream; this epic productizes the wiring, it does not invent a provider.

# Dashboard deploy-and-manage UI for the managed vector store

## Description

Adds the Dashboard integration for the managed vector store posture: a
deploy-and-manage UI through which administrators deploy and observe the
platform-managed Milvus vector store, delivering HLR-4 on the managed path.
Per the Dashboard architecture, the Dashboard reads and writes the component's
Kubernetes CRs and owns no data plane. Applies only if the platform-managed
posture is selected.

## Scope

- Surface the managed vector store in the Dashboard following the standard
  per-component integration pattern: navigation section, resource views, and
  deploy/manage actions over the operator's CR surface.
- Implement deployment and management interactions (deploy the managed store,
  view its status, delete it) against the CRs the Platform Operator defines for
  the managed vector store.
- Gate the integration behind the Dashboard's standard per-component feature
  flag mechanism (OdhDashboardConfig).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Dashboard exposes a deploy-and-manage UI for the managed vector store:
  an administrator can deploy the store, see its status, and delete it from
  the Dashboard without using raw YAML or the OpenShift console.
- The UI operates on the CR surface defined by the Platform Operator's managed
  vector store deployment capability.
- The integration is feature-flagged via the Dashboard's standard config CR
  and is off by default where the platform requires it.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): "The Dashboard exposes the chosen integration
  (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path)." — managed-path coverage.

## Notes

- Depends on the CR surface the Platform Operator's managed deployment
  defines; that surface must exist before the UI can be built against it.
- Runs in parallel with the Llama Stack provider wiring (different
  repositories, no shared artifacts).
